title: Classical limits and robust Gaussian coding gaps for compound bosonic fading channels
abstract: We study unassisted classical communication through memoryless mixtures of noisy, phase-insensitive bosonic Gaussian channels. Both thermal noise and photon budget scale with an energy parameter. An explicit measure-prepare representation converts every quantum block code, including entangled codewords and collective receivers, into a classical code with identical error and an exactly quantified cost increment. The same simulation works for an unknown fixed mixing law. A Gaussian-smoothing estimate and a uniform finite-alphabet reduction give an explicit O(E^-1) comparison with a classical compound variational value, optimizing one input law before taking the worst mixing law. For a matched-reset example we prove a strict separation from the time-sharing hull of Gaussian coherent modulations. Matching bounds determine the high-energy limit of a regularized Holevo functional with Gaussian average marginals. A block-uniform energy-controlled continuity modulus removes exact marginal Gaussianity and Gaussianity of the full average. Separate photon truncation and empirical moment concentration cover almost every product coherent Gaussian random codebook from a fixed finite deterministic schedule. Strict cost slack or an explicit common rescaling enforces physical feasibility. This yields an operational converse conditioned on reliability, below an unrestricted non-Gaussian common-code rate at sufficiently large energy. It neither constructs a good decoder for every random book nor covers every protocol described as Gaussian. The Gaussian, coding and continuity tools have established antecedents.
